executiveSummary: A confirmed cyberattack against North Carolina Ports disrupted gate operations and IT services across multiple facilities, forcing contingency procedures and creating immediate logistics delays. This remains the principal near-term maritime cyber risk in this cycle. Source Supporting Report Government advisories underscore persistent exposure from remotely serviceable maritime technology (e.g., ship-to-shore cranes), third-party access, and configuration/patch hygiene, elevating supply-chain and port-OT risk even absent specific new exploits. Government Advisory Research on space and satellite ecosystems highlights continuing risk to GNSS and satellite communications, which support maritime navigation and connectivity; exposed receivers and service disruptions could degrade bridge situational awareness if not mitigated. outlook72h: Analysts should monitor recovery progress at North Carolina Ports and watch for secondary congestion and scheduling impacts; additional official updates are likely. Source Supporting Report Given MARAD's advisory emphasis on vendor and remote-service exposure, additional scrutiny of third-party access pathways to port equipment is warranted; further advisories or operator notices may emerge. Government Advisory GNSS/satcom: Continued reporting on space-system cyber risks is likely; immediate maritime risk appears unchanged but warrants vigilance for interference anomalies.
